docs.title: 🛠 Unity Asset Store Contributions
docs.text: I publish editor tools and packages for other Unity developers, focused on workflow speed, modularity and reuse. They grew out of tooling I kept rebuilding across client projects.

docs.title: Products
docs.text:
• Script Dependency Viewer: an interactive node map of every C# script in a project.
  • WebGL Fullscreen Template: a WebGL template that makes builds fill the browser window.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Script Dependency Viewer is a Unity Editor tool that draws an interactive map of every C# script in a project's Assets folder. Each script is a movable, clickable node showing its name and namespace, laid out in a drag-and-zoom workspace.

Nodes can be coloured, edited live and used to jump straight to the code, which makes large or modular projects much easier to understand and maintain.

docs.title: What I Built
docs.text:
• A custom Editor window with a pannable, zoomable canvas.
  • Automatic discovery of all scripts in the project, with name and namespace parsing.
  • Node interactions: drag, select, colour-code and navigate to the script.
  • Packaging and submission to the Unity Asset Store, following its publishing guidelines.

docs.text: • Unity Asset Store

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A lightweight Unity WebGL template that makes the build canvas resize to fill the browser window, instead of Unity's default fixed-size frame.

docs.title: What I Built

• A custom WebGL template (HTML/CSS/JS) that scales the Unity canvas responsively with the browser window.
  • A drop-in package: import it, select the template in Player Settings, and build.

docs.title: BlackBlood
docs.text:
Fast. Stylish. Unforgiving.

Role: Solo Developer · Status: In active development · Scale: 350+ C# files

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: BlackBlood combines the gunplay of DOOM with the flashy combos of Devil May Cry. You survive intense combat arenas by constantly switching weapons and mixing melee and ranged attacks, and a live style rank rewards you for doing it well.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Seamless gun and melee combat, with switching mid-combo
  • Dynamic style ranking (D / C / B / A / S tiers)
  • Parkour movement: dash, wall-run and swing
  • Multiple melee and ranged weapons
  • More systems in progress

docs.title: What I Built
docs.text: I design, program and produce the whole game myself, including the combat, movement, weapon and style-ranking systems and the architecture that keeps a 350+ file codebase maintainable as a solo developer.

docs.title: Drone Strike VR
docs.text: Role: Unity Developer (sole developer)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A VR base-defence strategy game for Oculus Quest. Players protect their main tower from waves of enemy drones while attacking the opponent's key infrastructure.

  • Economy: an oil factory generates credits used to buy new assets. Credits carry over between levels.
  • Defence: radar improves drone detection, air defence shoots down incoming threats, and handheld weapons let the player fight directly.
  • Offence: precision-guided missiles and kamikaze drones target the enemy's radar, oil factory and air defence. Destroying them wins the level.
  • Progression: each level adds complexity and new weapons, and leaderboards score players on remaining oil and base damage.

The project was stopped before the end of production.

docs.title: Challenge
docs.text: I was the only developer on a project of this scale. With many moving units and simultaneous AI behaviours, performance problems built up quickly on the Quest's mobile hardware.

docs.title: What I Did
docs.text:
• Used Unity's profiling tools to find CPU bottlenecks, memory spikes and inefficient update loops.
  • Reworked the offending systems, which improved both stability and overall frame rate on device.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A small branded endless runner starring Goldy, the company's gorilla mascot, built in three days. Inspired by games like Subway Surfers, the player moves side to side, jumps and rolls to dodge rolling tree trunks around a spherical world.

docs.title: Challenge
docs.text: A tight three-day deadline, plus a procedural obstacle system that had to work on a spherical track.

docs.title: What I Did
docs.text:
• Planned the work into small, prioritised tasks to ship on time.

  • Object pooling: recycled obstacles once the player passed them, instead of creating and destroying them, which kept performance steady on mobile.

docs.title: Grândola AR
docs.text: Role: Unity Developer

docs.title: Client
docs.text: Grândola Municipality (Câmara Municipal de Grândola).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A marker-based AR app with animated scenes about the pottery process and Grândola's traditional culture.

docs.title: Challenge
docs.text: Keeping the AR content stable. When marker tracking flickered for a moment, models would disappear and pop back in, which broke the experience.

docs.title: What I Did
docs.text:
• Added a tracking grace period: when a marker is lost, the model stays at its last known pose for 3 seconds before hiding.
  • This removed the flicker caused by brief tracking drops while still hiding content when the marker was really gone.

docs.title: Grândola Mupi
docs.text: Role: Unity Developer

docs.title: Client
docs.text: Grândola Municipality (Câmara Municipal de Grândola).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A set of short educational games for an interactive mupi (a public touchscreen kiosk), all centred on Melides pottery: a clay game, an info game and a word search.

docs.title: Challenge
docs.text: The word search had to generate a new, valid puzzle every time, with words allowed to share letters where they cross.

docs.title: What I Did
docs.text:
I wrote a procedural word-search generator:

  1. For each word, pick a random direction (horizontal or vertical) and a valid start position for the word's length.
  2. Walk the cells: each one must be empty or already hold the same letter, so words can cross.
  3. If a placement fails, try a new position. After repeated failures, reset the grid and regenerate.
  4. Size the grid slightly larger than the longest word, which makes resets very rare in practice.
  5. Fill the remaining cells with random letters and render the grid.

docs.title: Grândola VR
docs.text: Role: Unity Developer

docs.title: Client
docs.text: Grândola Municipality (Câmara Municipal de Grândola).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A VR experience about the traditional craft of making clay pots. Players go through every step themselves, from gathering raw clay to shaping and finally selling the finished pot.

docs.title: Challenge
docs.text: It is a long, guided experience made of many sequential tasks. Each task needed a clear completion condition, visual cues to guide the player, and visual or audio feedback when it was done.

docs.title: What I Did
docs.text:
• Designed a task system: a manager that runs all the tasks in a scene and advances to the next one when the current task completes.
  • Built it on an abstract task base class, so each new task type plugs in with its own condition, hints and feedback while sharing the same flow.

docs.text: Role: Unity Developer

docs.title: Client

docs.text:
An augmented reality app for Android and iOS that showcases the client's product range. Users can:

docs.title: Challenge
docs.text: The app had to run on both iOS and Android, which meant supporting two different AR frameworks, ARKit and ARCore, in a single Unity project.

  • Integrated both into the same scene and adjusted them to coexist without conflicts.
  • Wrote a platform-detection layer that enables the right framework for iOS or Android.

docs.title: Super Bock Casa da Cerveja AR
docs.text: Role: Unity Developer

docs.title: Client
docs.text:
Super Bock is Portugal's best-selling beer brand worldwide, produced by the Super Bock Group since 1927.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Casa da Cerveja is a visitor tour inside the Super Bock Group production centre. This AR app brings the group's original brewing room back to life, walking visitors through the whole process: raw materials, wort production, fermentation, and bottling.

docs.title: Challenge
docs.text: The experience could only be tested on-site, in the museum. Placing 3D models accurately relative to the real room was slow and hard to iterate on.

docs.title: What I Did
docs.text:
• Built a developer placement tool that measured the device's position relative to the AR marker on-site and saved it.
  • Used those saved positions back in the studio to place models in the scene. It wasn't perfect, but it made the initial layout much faster and simpler.
